identity.real_world_identity_notes: AMS2 names the car Mitsubishi Lancer Evo10 RX, which establishes a simulator representation derived from the Lancer Evolution X. Mitsubishi's road-car material establishes the Evolution X identity but describes road transmissions that do not match the observed sequential-stick RX car. No official works or homologated rallycross Evolution X matching the AMS2 car was found, so no exact real build or year is asserted and the simulator's controls are not projected onto a real car.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was observed in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. The current two-stage downshift test found no automatic blip and the gear engaged without pedal input.
An older pre-fix drive reported automatic blip yes; both the corrected isolated recheck and this newer full drive returned no.

No matching real rallycross Evolution X was identified. The dogbox construction comes from the reviewed SuperCar category rule; the six ratios, sequential-stick mechanism and shift behavior remain simulator observations rather than claims about one exact real build.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mitsubishi-lancer-evo10-rx.20260822t040440382z-61781c99 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: The exact AMS2 identity and controls were observed live. Confidence is medium because research established the Evolution X basis but did not identify a corresponding works or homologated rallycross build.

claims.basis: The official AMS2 RX catalogue names Mitsubishi Lancer Evo10 RX, while Mitsubishi's manufacturer material establishes the Evolution X road model. No exact real rallycross implementation matching AMS2 was identified.

The guided drive selected six forward gears through a sequential stick. Mitsubishi's road-car transmissions do not support that RX configuration. The AMS2 entry is reviewed as an RX SuperCar-class representation: FIA Article 279 requires dog engagement and prohibits synchronisers and secondary clutch mechanisms, establishing the category's dogbox construction even though no exact real Evolution X build was identified. The six ratios and sequential-stick mechanism still come from the drive.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

deviations.basis: The AMS2 car is reviewed as an RX SuperCar-class representation, for which FIA Article 279 requires dog engagement and prohibits synchronisers and secondary clutch mechanisms. That establishes dogbox construction at category level despite no exact real Evolution X build being identified; the closest archetype instead carries gearbox_type sequential.

driver_summary: AMS2's Evolution X-derived RX car uses a six-speed sequential stick. Use the clutch to launch; it cuts flat clutchless upshifts and accepts coast downshifts without pedal work. No matching exact real rallycross build was identified.
